name: llasa
paper_title: LLaSA: A Sensor-Aware LLM for Natural Language Reasoning of Human Activity from IMU Data
authors: Sheikh Asif Imran, Mohammad Nur Hossain Khan, Subrata Biswas, Bashima Islam
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2406.14498 (cs.CL); also appeared in Companion of the 2025 ACM Int'l Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing (UbiComp/ISWC 2025 Companion)
license: Project website CC BY-SA 4.0; code repo license unknown (not verified)
notes: From BASH Lab, Worcester Polytechnic Institute. Compact sensor-aware LLM family (7B and 13B) that ingests raw IMU (accelerometer/gyroscope) data and produces natural-language, context-rich explanations / open-ended QA about human activity. Introduces two datasets: SensorCap (35,960 IMU-caption pairs) and OpenSQA (199,701 QA pairs, with a Tune-OpenSQA split). Reports outperforming GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o-mini on sensor-reasoning benchmarks. Earlier arXiv versions (v1/v2) titled 'LLaSA: Large Multimodal Agent...' / 'A Multimodal LLM for Human Activity Analysis Through Wearable and Smartphone Sensors'; current canonical title is the v3/v4 'Sensor-Aware LLM for Natural Language Reasoning...'. Datasets also mirrored on Google Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1128HH_idfgmZnDeqQV2rjFhm4-yW7HK7 . Published ACM version DOI: 10.1145/3714394.3756187. In HALO this is a DROPPED baseline (related work only; noted as slow in the data/baseline strategy).
